We ignore side effects of functions, meaning function calls do not modify their arguments.

Line 2: `String name = mapper.map(zipEntry.getName());` Here `name` depends on `zipEntry` because `zipEntry.getName()` is called and passed to `mapper.map`. So `name` depends on `zipEntry`.
Line 3: if (name != null) { ... }
Line 4: `File file = new File(outputDir, name);` So `file` is constructed using `name`. Since `name` depends on `zipEntry`, `file` depends on `zipEntry`.
Line 10: condition checks `name.indexOf("..")` etc., but that doesn't change `file`.
Line 14: if (zipEntry.isDirectory()) ... else block from line 17.
Line 18: `File tmp0 = file.getParentFile();` This uses `file`, but doesn't change `file`.
Line 19: `FileUtils.forceMkdir(tmp0);` side effect, ignore.
Line 21-23: logging, ignore.
Line 25: `FileUtils.copy(in, file);` Here `file` is used. The value of `file` at line 25 is the same `file` object created at line 4. So the value of `file` at line 25 depends on the value of `zipEntry` at line 1 because `file` was constructed from `name` which came from `zipEntry`.
